title: ALMA observations of the narrow HR 4796A debris ring
question: What are the radial and vertical structure of the HR 4796A debris ring at 880 um, is CO gas present, and what do these imply for dynamics and an interior planet?

data.sensitivity: 31 uJy/beam continuum; 2 mJy/beam per 0.42 km/s channel in cube

evidence.quote: an estimated stellar mass of 2.18 M$_{\odot}$ (cite: 1999A&AS..137..273G)

what.value: Scattered-light power-law indices and FWHM_r of 7 au

evidence.quote: the latter authors found $p_{\rm in} = 23$, and $p_{\rm out} = 13$ to $18$
The stellar emission is taken as that of a 9650K PHOENIX model atmosphere (cite: 2005ESASP.576..565B)

recipe.method: CLEAN imaging, phase self-cal, elliptical mask photometry
uvcontsub, natural-weight cube, velocity-shifted filtering over pixels >5 sigma in continuum
assumptions: CO co-located with dust; stellar mass 2.18 Msun

recipe.method: radmc-3d optically thin torus models, FT to uv points, chi2 minimisation with MCMC; Gaussian, box, power-law, eccentric variants
key_parameters: 40 walkers, 1000 steps, ~100 burn-in; data averaged to 10 s and four channels per SPW; weights recomputed with statwt; reweighting 1/2.5
assumptions: Dust size 10 um to 1 cm, q=11/6; 880 um opacity 0.17 m2/kg

recipe.goal: Convert CO flux limit to CO mass and ice fraction
recipe.method: NLTE statistical equilibrium over electron density and kinetic temperature, optically thin; photodissociation timescale; steady-state ratio to collisional mass loss rate
key_parameters: electron density 1e-3 to 1e12 cm-3; T 10 to 250 K
assumptions: Electrons main collider; CO optically thin

recipe.goal: Constrain interior planet from secular perturbations
recipe.method: Resonance overlap, secular precession and crossing-time criteria with Laplace coefficients

evidence.quote: we measure a total disk flux of $14.8 \pm 1.5$ mJy

answer_key.quantity: 12CO J=3-2 integrated flux upper limit (3 sigma)

evidence.quote: yields an integrated line flux upper limit (3$\sigma$) of 25 mJy km s$^{-1}$
is $p = 24 \pm 2$, which corresponds to a FWHM of only 5au
we therefore adopt 3.7 $\times$ 10$^{-6}$ M$_{\oplus}$ as the strict upper limit on the CO mass

evidence.loc: 4.2.2 Primordial origin of undetected CO excluded
evidence.quote: we derive a photodissociation timescale of eight years at the radial location of the ring’s centre

answer_key.quantity: CO+CO2 ice mass fraction upper limit

evidence.loc: 4.2.3 The CO+CO2 ice reservoir in HR 4796A’s exocomets
evidence.quote: upper limit of $<$1.8% on the CO+CO$_2$ ice mass fraction
The estimated mass loss rate is 26 $M_\oplus$ Myr$^{-1}$.
